name: nucleate_boiling_and_chf
title: Pool nucleate boiling heat flux and critical heat flux (function library)
summary: Twelve EES FUNCTIONs for the pool nucleate-boiling regime of a heated surface: nine heat-transfer-coefficient correlations (Rohsenow, McNelly, Forster-Zuber, Montinsky, Stephan-Abdelsalam with its five variants selected by one flag, HEDH-Taborek, Bier, Cooper, Gorenflo) returning h [W/m^2/K] from the excess wall temperature, and three critical-heat-flux correlations (Zuber, Serth-HEDH, HEDH-Montinsky) returning q_crit [W/m^2]. The fluid properties are arguments, so the calling model passes them; the wall heat flux follows from q = h*Te and the heat-transfer coefficient of the CHF correlations is left to the caller.

authors: H. K. Forster and N. Zuber (Forster-Zuber correlation)
I. L. Mostinsky (Montinsky and HEDH-Montinsky correlations)
K. Stephan and M. Abdelsalam (Stephan-Abdelsalam correlation)
Taborek (HEDH-Taborek correlation, as described by Schlunder)
E. U. Schlunder (VDI Heat Atlas, Gorenflo reference data and the HEDH presentation)
N. Zuber (Zuber critical heat flux and the Serth-HEDH form)
origin.notes: ht 1.2.0, commit 85e0ee6 (2025-12-07), file ht/boiling_nucleic.py, MIT license, Copyright (C) 2016 Caleb Bell. The scientific basis of each correlation is the original paper or book cited in its function comment block (mostly as given in Rohsenow, Hartnett & Cho, Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3E, McGraw-Hill, 1998, in Serth, Process Heat Transfer, 2E, 2014, and in Schlunder, Heat Exchanger Design Handbook, 1987 / VDI Heat Atlas, 1993). The ht data tables of reference coefficients h0 (h0_Gorenflow_1993, h0_VDI_2e) are not translated: h0 is an argument. Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3).

verification.reference: doctest values of ht 1.2.0 ht/boiling_nucleic.py (case A, incl. the five Stephan-Abdelsalam variants and both Zuber constants of the test suite) and additional values computed with the same ht functions in a throw-away virtualenv (case B); 32 output values in total
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 32 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); largest relative deviation 4.1e-11 (h_Cooper_A), i.e. round-off only.
